references.text: Jethro is first introduced here as the priest of Midian, and Moses becomes his son-in-law by marrying his daughter Zipporah.
Here Jethro is called Reuel/Reguel, Moses' father-in-law, and Moses tended his small livestock in Midian.
Moses asks his father-in-law Jethro for permission to return to Egypt.
Hobab, son of Reuel from Midian, Moses' father-in-law, is mentioned in connection with Israel's journey.
Describes what God did for Israel by delivering them from the Egyptians at the Red Sea - part of what Jethro heard about.
Prophesies that the nations, including Midian, will hear about the Lord's mighty deeds for Israel.
The victory over Amalek is one of the events God did for Israel that Jethro could have heard about.
The Lord brought the Israelites out of Egypt - the central event that Jethro heard about.
Moses reminds Israel that God brought them out of Egypt with mighty deeds.
Rahab tells that the people in Canaan had heard how the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt and dried up the Red Sea.
Complementary perspectives on the same event: Jethro's hearing of the news and Moses' confirmation of it.
Jethro's joyful response (18:9) is the direct theological conclusion to the news he heard in 18:1.
The sacrificial act in 18:12 is the natural liturgical response to the news of salvation in 18:1.
New Testament allusion that theologically summarizes and confirms the event of the Exodus mentioned in 18:1.
Historical retrospective confirming the Exodus as God's central act of salvation.
Allusion in Solomon's prayer linking the exodus to God's choice of Israel as His inheritance.
Parallel reference to the same salvation event: from the outside (Jethro) and from within (Israel's memory).
